page: Google Cloud Platform n4-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance configured with 2 vCPUs and 8.0 GB of RAM, yielding a 4.0 GB memory-to-core ratio. Built on the x86_64 architecture using Intel processors, this instance features 1 physical core with 2 threads per core via hyper-threading. The CPU allocation is dedicated, and the processor includes a cache hierarchy of 48 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 260 MB L3 cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for vector and matrix operations, alongside cryptographic acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities but limited multi-core scaling. The instance achieved a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1684.29 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1834.0. However, multi-core performance is constrained, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 1714.68 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 2251.0. Memory performance is also on the lower end, with uncached read and write large-block bandwidths measured at 19.35 GB/sec and 12.78 GB/sec respectively.

This instance does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, and it offers zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the n4-standard-2 provides a low-cost entry point for workloads requiring dedicated CPU allocation rather than shared-core burstable resources, though it presents performance tradeoffs in memory-intensive and highly parallelized tasks. It is best suited for lightweight general-purpose workloads, basic web serving, single-threaded text processing, and small-scale development or testing environments.
